text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.86% today after oil prices dropped sharply on news of diplomatic efforts between Iran and Saudi Arabia to de-escalate their conflict. The stock had jumped 3.8% on October 23rd when Middle East tensions peaked and oil hit six-month highs near $116 a barrel; today's decline reverses that trade as geopolitical risk recedes and crude falls back below $108 in the U.S. market.

The broader pattern here is straightforward: energy stocks track oil prices closely, and this week was a textbook example. Rising tensions and supply-disruption fears pushed oil up over a three-day span; renewed peace talks pushed it back down just as quickly. ConocoPhillips gained on the upside and is now giving some of those gains back as the immediate crisis narrative shifts.
